profiles.summary: Bold, dark and peppery. Warm regions give ripe, rich versions loaded with dark fruit, while cooler ones are more savoury, floral and restrained. In France it's called Syrah, in Australia Shiraz. Syrah and Shiraz are the exact same grape variety.
profiles.rag_text: Shiraz / Syrah (red grape). Bold, dark and peppery. Warm regions give ripe, rich versions loaded with dark fruit, while cooler ones are more savoury, floral and restrained. In France it's called Syrah, in Australia Shiraz. Syrah and Shiraz are the exact same grape variety. Body: Very full-bodied. Acidity: Medium. Tannin: Very firm. Sweetness: Dry. Alcohol: High (over 13.5%). Aromas: olive, smoke, violet, black pepper, blackberry. Flavours: dark fruit, spice, dark chocolate. Food pairings: barbecued ribs; lamb; sausages; hard cheese. Ageing: Good bottles improve over 5–15 years. Origin: Rhône Valley, France. Also known as: Syrah (France, Rhône); Shiraz (Australia). Key regions: Northern Rhône; Barossa; Victoria; Argentina; California; Chile; Washington State; Italy; New Zealand; South Africa; Switzerland; Spain.
